title: feat(cli): os migrate audit-side-copies runs the at-rest side-copy rewrite on the live audit tables and the archive
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-elon-musk"} -->
_Requested by **Elon** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01WedDzV26nniwxv7jC88B9D?thread=cmsg_01WedDzV26nniwxv7jC88B9DXuamRUC67fx2TTYrFfyuSH)_

Fixes #33155

Clause-②: yes (widening)
Metadata-protocol: none

## Maintainer quick read

- **What changed:** a new operator command, `os migrate audit-side-copies`, runs plugin-audit's at-rest side-copy rewrite (an approval request's `payload_json` removed from old audit and activity copies) on the live tables and on the archive. The rewrite's amendments now record that command as their name.
- **Why:** #33117 shipped the two rewrite functions with no way for an operator to run them, and its round-3 review left the name open until a door existed.
- **Risk and rollback:** low. The command is new, a dry run by default, and writes only with `--apply --yes`. Nothing runs it automatically. Rollback is reverting this PR; rows it already rewrote stay rewritten, as for its three twins.
- **Look first:** `packages/cli/src/commands/migrate/audit-side-copies.ts` (the `--object` refusal before the boot, and the two runner calls with `objects` and `seal`); `packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/side-copy-migration.ts` (the one-line name change); `packages/cli/src/commands/migrate/audit-side-copies.archive.integration.test.ts`.
- **Two-minute check:** `pnpm --filter @objectstack/cli exec vitest run --project integration src/commands/migrate/audit-side-copies.archive.integration.test.ts` shows 9 tests passing: dry run, `--object`, apply, re-run, archive, refusal.
- **What you need to do:** nothing; the seat lands it.

## What changes

- **`os migrate audit-side-copies`** (new, `packages/cli`). It runs `migrateSideCopies` on the live `sys_audit_log` and `sys_activity` rows, then `migrateArchivedSideCopies` on the archive datasource `sys_audit_log` archives to. It is a twin of `os migrate audit-key-material`, line for line: the read-only dry-run boot, the absent-table read view, the redaction seal (ADR-0154 D7), the archive classification (`examineArchiveTargets`) and the exit codes. Its flags are the same (`--database-url`, `--apply`, `--yes`, `--force`, `--json`), plus one more:
  - **`--object`**, repeatable, takes `sys_audit_log` or `sys_activity`. It narrows the hot run and the archive run to the tables it names; without it, both tables are walked. A name that is not a copy table is refused with the family's envelope, `OBJECT_NOT_FOUND` and exit 1, before the boot, so a typo never narrows a run to nothing.
  - **The report** gives, per copy table, the copies read (`scanned`), rewritten or to rewrite (`rewritten`) and sealed-and-refused (`refused`), for the hot store and for each archive. The `--json` document is `{ database, apply, objects, report, archive, duration }`. No line prints a value.
- **The rewrite's name** (`packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/side-copy-migration.ts`). A redaction amendment now records `rewritten_by: 'os migrate audit-side-copies'` instead of `side-copy-migration`.
- **Docs.** `content/docs/deployment/cli.mdx` gets a table row, a `#### os migrate audit-side-copies` section, and the command added to the read-only-boot and sealed-rows paragraphs. `content/docs/upgrading.mdx` gets an "Upgrading from 18.4.0 or earlier" line. The sibling migrations are documented in these two places; the plugin-audit README documents none of them.
- **Family rosters.** The new command joins every roster its twins sit in: `audit-redaction-seal.contract.test.ts`, `migrate-confirmation-exit.pin.test.ts`, `json-stdout-purity.e2e.test.ts`, `schema-migrate.one-shot-family.integration.test.ts`, and `data-commands.absent-database.integration.test.ts` (with a seeded live `sys_activity` copy, so the hot activity path is driven too).

### The name, and why

Round 3 of the #33117 contract review said: "The rewrite records its amendments as `side-copy-migration`; the two precedents record the command name (`os migrate audit-key-material`, `os migrate audit-mail-bodies`). Settle the name when the door lands."

- **Command name `audit-side-copies`.** The three siblings are named `audit-` plus what they rewrite: `audit-metadata-bodies`, `audit-mail-bodies`, `audit-key-material`. This rewrite removes the columns of the list `side-copy-columns.ts` holds (`SIDE_COPY_COLUMNS`), as `audit-key-material` removes the list `key-material-copy.ts` holds. `audit-approval-payloads` would name the only entry today, but the list is keyed by object and built to take more, so the name follows the list.
- **Amendment name `os migrate audit-side-copies`.** All three precedents record the full command (`os migrate audit-...`) as `rewritten_by`, so an operator reading `sys_audit_amendment` finds the command to re-run. The old name never shipped in a release: #33117's changeset is still pending. A row amended on a pre-release build keeps the old name, which the changeset says.
- **ADR-0154 slice P4b3** will make `os migrate audit-* --apply` hold a database session lock. This command matches that pattern and takes the same `--apply` path as its twins, so P4b3 covers it with no special case. This PR builds no lock.

## Tests

Every new pin was run red before the code existed. The command file was held out of the tree, and plugin-audit still recorded the old name.

- **Red, at `0c23193ab` (tests only):**
  - `audit-side-copies.archive.integration.test.ts`: 7 failed, all with `Error: command migrate:audit-side-copies not found`. Test 7 ("no run prints a sentinel") passed, as it must when nothing runs.
  - `audit-redaction-seal.contract.test.ts`: failed with `ENOENT ... audit-side-copies.ts`.
  - `audit-seal-redaction-live.integration.test.ts`: 1 failed, 16 passed. Expected `"os migrate audit-side-copies"`, received `"side-copy-migration"`.
- **Green, at `34582583d`:**
  - `audit-side-copies.archive.integration.test.ts`, 9 cases:
    - 0: the fixture is real (the real Archiver moved 3 copies, 2 of them carrying the column).
    - 1: dry run. Per table, hot `sys_audit_log` 1 scanned / 1 to rewrite and archive 2 / 2. Both stores are byte-identical afterwards.
    - 1b: the human face prints the same counts per table and per store.
    - 2: `--object sys_activity --apply` reads only `sys_activity`, has no archive entry, and leaves both stores unchanged.
    - 3: `--apply` leaves 0 carrying copies in either store and reports what it wrote. Every other key, column and the unlisted object's row is unmoved.
    - 4: the re-run rewrites nothing.
    - 5: the copy that was hot when the command ran is archived clean.
    - 6: `--object sys_approval_request` is refused with `OBJECT_NOT_FOUND`, exit 1.
    - 7: no sentinel is printed.
  - `data-commands.absent-database.integration.test.ts`: the new door answers empty work on a missing database, and on the booted control it rewrites 1 `sys_audit_log` and 1 live `sys_activity` copy.
  - `schema-migrate.one-shot-family.integration.test.ts`: the dry run writes nothing and `--apply` behaves as its family does.
  - The live amendment pin: a sealed approval-request copy is amended, rewritten, and reads `redacted` under `rewritten_by: 'os migrate audit-side-copies'`.

No separate ablation was run. The red run above is the before-and-after for each pin: the behaviour is new, and the same files go from red to green with only the implementation added.

## Acceptance notes

- `sys_activity` declares no archive target, so `--object sys_activity` reports `archive: []`. Case 2 pins that.
- The archive classification the twins share (`none` / `not-connected` / `unknown`) is pinned in `audit-key-material.archive.integration.test.ts` and `audit-mail-bodies.archive.integration.test.ts`. It is not repeated here, because this command calls the same `examineArchiveTargets`.
- `docs/adr/0154-...md` lists the three earlier rewrites by command. It is not edited here: the ADR is a decision record, not a roster.

## Verification

All readings are at head `34582583d` (worktree cut from `origin/main` `4bba8b8f0`).

  - The 2 failures are `test/published-subpath-console.pin.test.ts` and `test/published-subpath-hook-body.pin.test.ts`. Both refused with "packages/cli is not built (./dist/index.js is absent)", a missing-prerequisite refusal, not a finding. The closure build does not build `packages/cli` itself. The touched `migrate-confirmation-exit.pin.test.ts` and `audit-redaction-seal.contract.test.ts` are in the 418 that passed.

  - 96 exited 0.
  - 7 exited 3 (PREREQUISITE NOT MET, so NOT MEASURED here). CI runs each on a built tree:
    - `check:i18n`, `check:i18n-coverage`, `check:i18n-walk-parity`, `check:type-check-debt`: "the workspace CLI is not built".
    - `check:dual-build-cjs-loads`: a package with no `dist/`.
    - `spec check:skill-examples`: client-react not built.
    - `check-plugin-teardown-shape --self-test`: the shallow clone cannot reach its pinned fixture.
